summary: Internal SE enablement focused on messaging, competitive positioning, and demo practice. Covered elevator pitches for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, common objections (latency vs cost, on-prem/regulatory needs), and practiced two demo flows. Identified gaps in pricing language and need for clearer fallback scripts for degraded capacity situations.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private tradeoffs
transcript: 00:00:00 Header: Date: 2027-06-02 | Start: 10:00 AM PT | Duration approx 60m | Attendees: Priya, Liam, Sofia, Jake, Maya, Tom
00:00:12 Priya: Alright, hey everyone thanks for joining today's SE enablement, gonna run through some messaging and then Liam will do a demo run. Sorry if the audio is a little off, I'm on hotspot
00:00:28 Liam: Hey all, quick agenda: 1) messaging refresh, 2) competitive talk tracks, 3) demo practice, 4) Q&A and next steps, cool?
00:00:37 Jake: Yep sounds good, want to make sure we get the handoff playbook for the AE
00:00:43 Sofia: I'll drop the one-pager after the call, and added a slide on pricing tiers, there may be a typo in the Dedicated section in the deck you saw (it says 'Dedicates'), will fix

00:01:10 Priya: Nice catch. Ok quick messaging: lead with production-first premise — predictable latency, cost controls, and deployment flexibility. Two-sentence pitch: Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLMs predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, so you can ship faster without building the whole stack.
00:02:05 Tom: Quick question — do we lead with performance or with compliance for enterprise buyers?

00:02:14 Priya: Depends on the persona. For platform/infra buyers -> performance/cost. For security/compliance -> privacy and KMS, SOC2, audit logs. Have both bullets ready and flip based on stakeholder, yep

00:03:05 Liam: Competitive framing: OpenAI is often positioned as easiest for devs, but we call out that we provide a consistent runtime across environments (hosted/dedicated/private) and stronger observability and SLA options. Anthropic shows up on safety messaging; acknowledge their strengths but push Redwood's deployment flexibility and cost controls.
00:04:10 Jake: What about Bedrock? Customers ask about cloud-native integration and vendor lock-in
00:04:20 Sofia: For Bedrock, emphasize our model catalog + neutral runtimes and ability to run private deployments in customer VPCs or on-prem — less lock-in and better control over data residency.

00:05:02 Priya: Role play quick objection: 'We can't move to dedicated because it's too expensive' — response: show unit economics, batching + KV cache saves, and Redwood Optimize recommendations. Offer a pilot on hosted to measure real token costs before a dedicated commit.
00:06:20 Maya: People ask about quantization and latency — how deep do we go?

00:06:28 Liam: SEs should cover high-level: quantization options, tradeoffs (accuracy vs throughput), and that runtime picks kernels automatically. If they want deep dive, we do technical deep dive with Research/Infra and reference our perf benchmarks.

00:07:45 Priya: Demo flow — two variants: quick 5-min exec demo and 20-min technical demo. For exec: show integrated API, simple prompt, cost dashboard. For technical: show dedicated pool config, autoscaling, and a trace of a high-throughput request plus fallback policy.
00:08:30 Liam: I'll run the 20-min demo now. Note: I'll hit the demo account which is pre-populated; if latency seems weird it's because of my laptop wifi, ignore micro stutters.

00:08:50 Liam: (starts screen) Opening Console -> Models -> show catalog. Note: transcript might read model name wrong like 'g-p three' instead of correct repo name, ignore that, it's auto transcript glitch.

00:10:12 Liam: Walking through Dedicated config: pool size, reserved vCPU/GPU, autoscale policy, burst capacity. Show commit terms. Emphasize SLA and predictable throughput for customers with steady workloads.
00:12:40 Tom: For procurement questions, do we have standard contract SLAs or is it negotiable?
00:12:48 Priya: We have standard SLA tiers; for enterprise deals we work with legal to customize but baseline is consistent, refer to legal playbook and get procurement involved early.

00:14:05 Liam: Demo continues: show routing policy — can route by latency or cost, automatic fallback to quantized variant if primary model is overloaded. This is a strong differentiator vs many managed endpoints that don't have variant fallbacks.
00:15:30 Maya: Can we show an example of KV cache hit rate?
00:15:38 Liam: Yes quick screenshot of observability dashboard — token-level breakdown, cache hit/miss, per-route latency. I'll upload that to enablement folder after call.

00:17:22 Priya: Role play: customer says 'we need on-prem air gap' — response: yes we support Private with on-prem packages and control plane options, plus KMS/HSM integrations. Capture compliance artifacts (SOC2, ISO) and send security docs.
00:18:55 Sofia: Note for AE talk track: when security is primary, lead with Private, then expand to Dedicated for predictable costs, and Hosted only for early POCs where speed is priority.
00:20:02 Liam: Demo practice: Liam plays SE, Tom plays AE, Jake plays customer. Start quick exec demo: prompt -> streaming response -> cost widget -> fallback policy described.
00:22:10 Tom: (role-play) 'We're worried about hallucinations' — how to respond?

00:22:18 Priya: Admit the risk, talk about evals, prompt sets, Redwood Optimize monitors quality, suggest a prompt engineering engagement and eval harness for regression alerts. Offer canary rollout and A/B testing to measure quality.
00:24:03 Maya: A bit of transcription noise here, 'KV cash' appears in the notes instead of 'KV cache', just a reminder these auto transcriptions are imperfect

00:25:40 Liam: Practiced handoff: AE collects business metrics and scale estimates, SE proposes config and pilot metrics, legal/procurement loop for dedicated commitments. We wrote a playbook (link shared) — I'll repost.

00:27:55 Priya: Competitive rebuttal bank quick hits: 1) OpenAI - faster dev but less enterprise control; 2) Anthropic - safety heavy but less deployment modes; 3) Bedrock - good cloud fit but potential lock-in. Keep these short and situational.
00:30:10 Sofia: We noticed the pricing slide confuses some reps — need to add explicit examples (50k tokens/day, cost delta hosted vs dedicated). I'll add a worked example.
00:32:00 Jake: Any tips on demo pacing? New AEs rush through console which confuses buyers.

00:32:08 Liam: Slow down, narrate expected outcomes, and always call out the cost/latency tradeoff. Use our two scripts: 'Executive' for 5 minutes and 'Technical' for deep dives. Link to scripts in Confluence.

00:34:45 Priya: Wrap-up recap: share deck, competitive one-pager, demo recording, and the playbook. Next immediate action items are in the chat and I'll follow up with calendar invites for practice sessions.
00:35:10 Tom: Quick legal note: if customer demands data residency in EU, mention Private or Dedicated in EU region and capture as requirement in CRMs.
00:36:55 Maya: Thanks everyone. Two asks from me: can we get the demo recording and the sample prompt sets used in the demo?
00:37:07 Liam: Yup will upload both, will label clearly. Also fixing a bunch of typos in the deck and the Dedicated spelling, ha.
00:38:30 Priya: Closing — thanks for practicing, Matt and others who couldn't make it we'll record and share. End call.
